A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a conformal field theory, the correlator of four scalar operators of equal scaling dimensions is a conformally invariant function of two pairs of ratios.

we have provided a new tool for computing conformal correlators, which is complementary to the existing techniques, and which is particularly useful when the correlators have a large number of kinematical variables.
we have found the analog of KKR for correlators of 4 scalar operators, and we have computed the kernel explicitly.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Lorentz inversion formula and dispersion relations provide a complete description of the four-point function in conformal field theory, and that they can be used to obtain exact results for correlators.
the dispersion relation can be used to extract the absorptive part of correlators from the conformal blocks.
conformal blocks can be computed in two different ways: either by summing the data of the Lorentz inversion formula, or by integrating the data of the dispersion relation.
